title: The morning before
rule: The day from dawn to four is compressed into the top two tiers; the incident itself fits in the bottom tier.
declares: adds the morning (how the memo came): a man off the 7:40 leaves word from the Division that a freight inspector comes at 4:15 and the SERVICE door must be open; the agent writes the memo; E0-E5 keep the canon in the bottom tier
made: three tier cards on the LoC 1934 sheet: tier 1 'First light to noon' (cool grey-blue), tier 2 'Noon to four' (warm), tier 3 '4:08 to 4:11' (the kit's butter card); tier titles in the kit's jumping cover lettering (shared pen hand)

tier 1, four press prints with white scissor margins: 5:50 the empty office at first light (99-ways-template office plate, Rothstein 1937 with the clerk removed, toned cold and dim); 7:40 the Agence Rol 1933 double-deck carriage; 7:42 the ticket window from inside with the Rol 49112 man behind the glass and his order in a balloon ('From the Division: freight inspector at 4:15. Have the SERVICE door open.', ours); 7:50 the memo being pencilled (Rothstein P1 rest layers, close on the slip)

tier 2: 12:00 the empty desk (office plate, warm) with a pasted pen-lettered memo slip by the inkwell; 2:12 the Rol 57642 walking man as a free cutout with a ticket stub 'RANDOLPH to MONTPELIER'; 3:55 the agent at the TICKET OFFICE window (Rothstein P4 rest layers)

on every tier-1/2 piece the office clock cut out from the 99-ways-template LoC clock pieces with its own hands re-set on the arbor to that hour (5:50, 7:40, 7:42, 7:50, 12:00, 2:12, 3:55): the hands race through the day

tier 3: E0-E5 in six narrow press prints of the 99-ways-template rest layers P1, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8, red numbers 1-6, the Agence Rol 34852 stranger behind the glass in E1 and E3, the four canon lines in the shared cut-paper balloons, caption slips and clock times 4:08-4:11

tier1.caption: First light. He unlocks the office and winds the clock.
The 7:40 stops two minutes: milk cans, one mailbag.
A man off the train leaves word at the window.
He pencils it on a memo slip. Key in the cupboard.

tier2.caption: Noon. Dinner at the desk. The memo waits by the inkwell.
Tickets for the 2:12: a gentleman for Montpelier.
Five to four. Quiet. The memo before him.

tier3.caption: He sets off for the key.
A lady at the window:
tier3.balloon: Pardon me — have you the right time?

tier3.caption: He looks at the clock:
tier3.balloon: Ten past four, by the clock.

tier3.caption: And there he stands.
tier3.balloon: Well, here I am... and what for?

events.E0: tier 3 print 1: at the desk with the memo (4:08), 'He sets off for the key.'
events.E1: tier 3 print 2: the stranger behind the TICKET OFFICE glass, question balloon (4:09)
events.E2: tier 3 print 3: he looks up at the clock (4:10 in the print), answer balloon
events.E3: tier 3 print 4: she turns from the window, thanks balloon (4:10)
events.E4: tier 3 print 5: the cupboard open, the key on its hook with the SERVICE tag (4:11)
events.E5: tier 3 print 6: pencil to his chin, forgetting balloon (4:11)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the day is laid down piece by piece, each print with its clock re-set further on (5:50 ... 3:55); then the six incident prints are laid in the bottom tier two at a time

self_check.evidence: perceptually judged (from frames) by the maker at full size; independent blind readers not yet run
self_check.check: A reader finds E0-E5 only in the bottom tier: tiers 1-2 hold only the day before 4:00 (5:50 to 3:55, no stranger, cupboard closed); the six numbered tier-3 prints hold E0-E5 and the four lines
self_check.outcome: key on its hook in print 5; nothing in print 6 opens the SERVICE door
